purpose: Independent practice of A9.2 — identifying 3D shapes and distinguishing them from 2D. Used as Lesson 2 consolidation artifact and as evidence for the formative tracker.
student_learning_goal: I can identify and describe 3D shapes.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can identify and describe 3D shapes.
header.character_watermark: Mira the Map-Making Monkey in the top-right corner of the header, holding a compass. Small (~1.5in tall). References the shared 'Mira the Map-Making Monkey' asset from blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Draw a line from each 3D shape to its name.
parts.visual_layout: A two-column matching activity centred on the page. Left column shows 5 3D shape pictures rendered with light shading to suggest depth (sphere, cube, cylinder, cone, pyramid), each ~1.3in tall, stacked vertically. Right column shows 5 names ('sphere', 'cube', 'cylinder', 'cone', 'pyramid') in scrambled order, also stacked. A wide gap between columns invites the student to draw connecting lines.

image_placeholders.description: Five 3D shape thumbnails arranged in a vertical column for a Kindergarten matching activity. From top to bottom: sphere (round ball with a single shading line), cube (showing 3 faces), cylinder (with curved top edge), cone (with a circular base), pyramid (square base, 4 triangular faces). Each shape ~1.3in tall, B&W with light shading to convey depth, generous spacing for line-drawing.
image_placeholders.placement: Left column of Part 1, vertically centred.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P1_SHAPES at left column of Part 1: the 3D shape names listed in the right column (sphere, cube, cylinder, cone, pyramid) match the visual shapes. Each keyword names a shape that the student must see and identify.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each shape. Write 2D under the FLAT shapes. Write 3D under the SOLID shapes.
parts.visual_layout: A 2×4 grid of 8 shape thumbnails centred on the page, each cell ~1.5in square. Shapes shown alternate between 2D and 3D: circle, sphere, square, cube, triangle, pyramid, rectangle, cylinder. Below each shape is a label line for the child to write '2D' or '3D'. 3D shapes are drawn with light shading; 2D shapes are flat outlines.

image_placeholders.description: An eight-cell shape grid in B&W line art arranged in 2 rows of 4. Top row left to right: circle (flat outline), sphere (shaded ball), square (flat outline), cube (3 faces visible). Bottom row left to right: triangle (flat outline), pyramid (3D, square base), rectangle (flat outline), cylinder (3D with curved edge). Each cell ~1.5in square; below each shape is a label line for the child to write '2D' or '3D'.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P2_GRID at Part 2: instructions ask the child to identify FLAT (2D) vs SOLID (3D). Visual alternates 2D and 3D shapes; keywords name each shape so the child sees which is flat (circle, square, triangle, rectangle) vs solid (sphere, cube, pyramid, cylinder).

parts.answer_key: 2D (flat): circle, square, triangle, rectangle. 3D (solid): sphere, cube, pyramid, cylinder.

parts.part_title: Part 3: Find 3D shapes in your classroom!
parts.student_instructions: Look around your classroom. Find 3 things that are 3D. Draw each one. Write the 3D shape name beside your drawing.
parts.visual_layout: Three rows of two-column workspaces stacked vertically. Each row has a left column with a blank 2in × 1.5in drawing box (thin border) and a right column with a label line '__________ shape' for writing the 3D shape name. To the right of all three rows, a small reference column lists the 5 3D names stacked vertically: sphere, cube, cylinder, cone, pyramid.

image_placeholders.description: Three blank drawing boxes stacked vertically for a Kindergarten worksheet. Each box is ~2in wide × 1.5in tall, with a thin solid border. Beside each box, a horizontal line for writing the 3D shape name. Suitable for the child to draw a 3D classroom object (e.g., ball, can, dice) and label its 3D shape (sphere, cylinder, cube).
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS02_P3_BOXES at Part 3: instructions ask the child to find 3 3D things in their classroom and draw them. The blank boxes provide drawing workspace; the keywords name the 3D shapes the child must identify (ball=sphere, dice=cube, can=cylinder, etc.).

parts.answer_key: Any 3 valid examples. Common: ball=sphere, dice/Rubik's cube=cube, soup can=cylinder, party hat/pylon=cone, building block=cube or pyramid. Accept any reasonable answer where the 3D shape name matches the object's primary form.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, find 1 more 3D shape outside your classroom. Where do you see it?
teacher_notes: Lesson 2 consolidation artifact. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Most children should complete Parts 1 and 2 with one prompt. For Part 3, accept any valid match between drawing and 3D shape name. Use Part 2 as the formative evidence for distinguishing 2D vs 3D — this is the key signal for whether the child holds the flat-vs-solid distinction. Children who confuse 2D and 3D in Part 2 likely need a hands-on re-loop with real 3D models before moving to Lesson 3.
